title: CLEVR is the best Mendix-cohort conversion target: right size and lineage, wrong incumbent
content:
The screen reads CLEVR as right on the two attributes it usually weights most heavily — size (250+ staff) and lineage — and wrong on the one that overrides them: the incumbent. Its published stack is Mendix and Siemens, which means the app layer a Powerhouse engagement would sit in is already occupied by a proprietary platform the firm sells for a living. That is what puts a well-matched Dutch integrator at priority 9, do not pitch.

The mechanism is commercial rather than technical. A partner's platform relationship is not a neutral technology preference; it is the basis on which the delivery business is priced and staffed. A firm earning against Mendix licences and Mendix-certified developers has no reason to carry a typed-spec alternative into the same account, because the alternative competes with the thing that pays for the bench.

What the assessment does add is a ranking inside the excluded set: CLEVR is the best of the Mendix cohort if conversion is ever pursued. That is a different, slower motion from partnership — it asks the firm to trade a platform relationship rather than add a layer beside it. Read practically, CLEVR is the first name to call if a conversion programme gets funded, and nothing to do before then.
